A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BioReason and retain matching architecture, datasets, experiments, and case-study material. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original model evaluations on KEGG disease prediction and two variant-effect benchmarks in Tables 1–2, plus a generated biological reasoning case study.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds GRPO training curves, chromatin-accessibility experiments, and per-disease KEGG results in the appendices.

M1.justification: The core frozen-DNA-encoder, linear-projection, and Qwen architecture remains. V2 switches the reported reinforcement-learning procedure to Dr. GRPO, simplifies five reward components to three, and changes the conciseness threshold from four to ten words. Section 3.3 also replaces separator-interleaved DNA embeddings with direct stacking. These revise components within the retained framework.

E1.justification: The original KEGG, VEP-Coding, and VEP-Non-SNV coverage remains. Appendix B adds an evaluated chromatin-accessibility task using DeepSEA-derived data across 20 DNase-seq tracks and diverse cell types, substantially extending coverage beyond variant and disease prediction.

E2.justification: Appendix B/Table 3 adds an evaluated Enformer DNA-only baseline with frozen weights and a trained attention head. The original NT, Evo2, and Qwen comparison methods remain. Newly cited ChatNT and rbio1 are discussed as related work but are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: V2 extends RL evaluation to both 4B hybrids and introduces a held-out, multilabel chromatin-accessibility protocol using 200-bp bins and macro/weighted metrics. Appendix A.1 also reports GRPO-specific settings replacing v1's shared defaults, including learning rate 1e-5 versus 5e-5 and LoRA rank 16 versus 32. These are reported setting revisions; the PDFs do not establish which existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands analysis through SFT-versus-GRPO comparisons for both 4B hybrids, training-dynamics comparisons across three configurations in Appendix A.5, and per-disease results for ten KEGG categories in Appendix C. These examine RL effectiveness, convergence, and performance heterogeneity. The original PFN1 case study is retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report seed 23. V2 newly discloses single experimental runs in checklist item 7 and describes Figure 4's shading as per-step reward variance across eight generations per query. Benchmark confidence intervals, significance tests, and between-run variability estimates remain absent.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises retained results: Qwen3-4B accuracy changes from 93.48% to 90.00%, and Evo2+Qwen3-4B SFT from 97.24% to 95.17%. Both newly reported 4B+GRPO configurations reach 98.28%. Table 3 adds chromatin results, including macro F1 of 33.70% for Enformer+Qwen3-4B versus 17.18% for Enformer; Table 4 adds disease-level results. Table 2 is unchanged. Revised RL training prevents interpreting its cross-version scores as same-setting gains.

T1.justification: Appendix A.4, Equation 3 changes the advantage definition from reward minus group mean divided by group standard deviation to mean-centering alone. This is a substantive mathematical revision, although the surrounding prose still mentions standard deviation. The likelihood and clipped-objective equations remain, with no new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract changes its headline KEGG comparison from 88%–97% to 86%–98% and confines the average 15% gain statement to variant-effect tasks. The introduction qualifies the integration priority claim with 'large' DNA models and removes superiority over 'simple combination' approaches. The principal multimodal reasoning and interpretability contributions remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive interpretations concerning larger backbones' greater RL benefit, convergence and optimization stability, supervised versus unsupervised encoder transferability, and performance beyond frequent disease categories. Section 6 also explicitly identifies lost distal genomic context as a consequence of the retained 2048-token truncation limit.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 substantially expands reproducibility information with separate SFT/GRPO configurations, cosine scheduling and warmup, eight generations, 1000 training steps, model-specific sampling temperatures, top-p/top-k, and explicit clipping and KL coefficients. Section 5.3 newly identifies vLLM inference. The existing code/data/checkpoint availability statement is retained.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 now acknowledges ChatNT as a prior integration of DNA-model representations with language models and distinguishes BioReason through training for complex biological reasoning. This materially revises positioning against closely related work. Added citations also cover rbio1, Dr. GRPO, scientific reasoning, Enformer, and DeepSEA.

P1.justification: V2 makes targeted rewrites to the abstract, related work, results, limitations, and conclusion while preserving the main section sequence and much of the prose. It reorganizes training details into SFT/GRPO blocks and adds appendix subsections, acknowledgments, conference identification, and a NeurIPS checklist.

P2.justification: V2 substantially extends the visual evidence with an uncertainty-shaded training-curve figure, a chromatin-accessibility comparison table, and a grouped per-disease results table. Table 1 is expanded and regrouped into SFT/GRPO comparisons. The original architecture, dataset, and PFN1 figures retain their content.

improvement.justification: The added chromatin-accessibility evaluation, RL analyses, explicit training settings, and acknowledgment of ChatNT improve empirical breadth, reproducibility, and positioning. These gains are limited by single-run evaluations and unspecified split sizes for the new benchmark. V2 also introduces an internal inconsistency: Appendix A.3's reward components sum to 3.0, while A.3 and A.5 state a maximum of 2.5. The added evidence and documentation support a limited net improvement despite these reporting weaknesses.
